NOTE: CNBC (20 Jul). Brent closed Monday +1.3% at $89.22/bbl; WTI +0.9% at $83.23. Brent had jumped nearly 4% overnight to break $90 before easing when Iran FM spokesman Baghaei signalled negotiations possible. Prices up ~20% this month. Houthis declared maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia Monday. US petrol back to $4/gallon (AAA). Amrita Sen (Energy Aspects): slowdown in Hormuz traffic + depleted inventories could push oil above $100; "The market is still quite complacent despite the price increase." TUESDAY (via Reuters wire, reuters.com/business/energy/oil-prices-dip-mediation-efforts-offset-us-iran-strikes-2026-07-21/, cross-ref investinglive + TradingEconomics): Brent fell ~78 cents/0.9% to ~$88.44 by 0415 GMT, WTI ~$82.50, as 10-day ceasefire reports offset escalation; oil holding near one-month highs.
